evidence.claim: Three planted duplicate classes (exact-duplicate, paraphrase, one-parameter-fork) each have recall 1.0 under the two-signal counter; the nine members collapse to three unique mechanisms.
Six distinct-mechanism representatives produce unique_count=6 and false-merge rate 0 on all C(6,2)=15 pairs.

negative_controls.description: A pure string-equality counter must score worse on the planted set (higher unique count / lower mean per-class recall), proving the semantic layer contributes.
Signal A (char n-gram Jaccard, no synonyms) and Signal B (parameter-stripped skeleton with synonym fold) disagree on planted XOR pairs, so they are not the same predicate.

signals.A: character-4gram Jaccard on alnum-folded text; threshold 0.36; no synonym table
signals.B: frozenset equality of tokens after dropping numerics/units and applying a small synonym fold; min 3 tokens
signals.blind_spot: full rewrite with neither n-gram overlap nor synonym-covered tokens
signals.merge_rule: same mechanism iff A OR B fires
